method: Parallel read-only source review across application, DB, configuration, native transport, security boundaries and CI; inspected historical evidence without rerunning it. No tests/builds/probes/Cargo/validators/fixture capture/dependency updates or fresh advisory scans.

batches.title: Registration flow and Followup URL handling
DNS external-record reload and JSON receiver

findings.title: Followup loses precedence to a supplied auth key
findings.impact: A registration carrying both Followup and Auth.AuthKey can redeem the key instead of waiting for its existing interactive authorization.
findings.next_action: Select Followup after existing-node handling and before auth-key redemption, matching pinned handler order.

findings.title: Followup URL/path grammar differs
findings.impact: Escaped paths and extra path prefixes can produce different registration-ID acceptance and errors. Machine binding is a separate control and remains present.
findings.next_action: Use native Go URL parsing, decoded Path and selected registration-ID transformation together with F01.

findings.title: OIDC provider identifier serialization differs
findings.impact: Manual URL splitting can persist a different provider_identifier, changing imported account lookup, owner continuity and policy references. Example source projection: a space in a subject is escaped by Go URL.String and left raw by Rust.
findings.next_action: Port the selected CleanIdentifier parse/clean/serialize behavior at the native identity boundary without changing public field types.

findings.title: OIDC email admission differs
findings.impact: The simple rsplit-at/no-whitespace check accepts malformed values such as a@@example.com that Go mail.ParseAddress rejects; the result enters persisted user/profile and policy identity state.
findings.next_action: Implement selected mailbox parsing/admission and preserve original accepted claim text as Go does.

findings.title: OIDC username character categories differ
findings.impact: Rust Unicode alphabetic/numeric predicates and first-character handling differ from the selected Go byte-first check plus IsLetter/IsDigit. Persisted name and policy-alias outcomes can differ.
findings.next_action: Share one pinned native username predicate for OIDC profile publication; do not infer Go categories from Rust generic predicates.

findings.title: OIDC callback repeated-query handling differs
findings.impact: Serde struct extraction rejects repeated code/state before the handler; Go URL.Query().Get selects the first value. This changes acceptance/status, with no demonstrated authentication bypass.
findings.next_action: Decode native callback queries using selected first-value/escape rules while retaining state, nonce and CSRF checks.

findings.title: DNS extra-record changes can remain stale
findings.impact: The five-second watcher only reloads on changed mtime. A write preserving mtime can be missed indefinitely; Go reacts to write/create/chmod and re-establishes replacement watches.
findings.next_action: Replace mtime-only admission with equivalent event/rewatch semantics and content-aware recovery in one file-reload batch.

findings.title: DNS extra-record JSON receiver differs
findings.impact: Root null, empty objects, case-folded field names, null strings and duplicate-last assignment differ from Go decoding; supported startup/reload files can be rejected.
findings.next_action: Apply selected Go JSON receiver semantics to file-backed records together with watcher changes, preserving empty/transient-read behavior.

findings.title: Configured DNS resolver URL validation is incomplete
findings.impact: Rejecting only SocketAddr accepts malformed URL input such as https://% that Go ignores. Both global and split resolver projection are affected.
findings.next_action: Use ParseAddr-or-successful-Go-URL admission and selected diagnostics for both resolver paths.

findings.title: NextDNS query parsing/encoding differs
findings.impact: Malformed escape and semicolon pairs are retained, and invalid decoded bytes are replaced by UTF-8 lossiness, whereas Go Query/Encode drops malformed pairs and preserves decoded bytes.
findings.next_action: Reuse a byte-preserving native query parser/encoder rather than another bespoke string implementation.

findings.title: Nil Hostinfo changes NextDNS device_model
findings.impact: Imported NULL Hostinfo is projected to an empty OS and then overwrites/adds device_model; Go leaves that query key alone when Hostinfo is invalid.
findings.next_action: Retain Hostinfo presence through requester projection and update metadata conditionally.

findings.title: DERP URL/map loading has different admission rules
findings.impact: Invalid configured URLs abort rather than log-and-skip; error-status bodies containing valid maps are rejected; lowercase JSON regions is missed; YAML region defaults/mismatches are changed or rejected rather than preserving decoded values.
findings.next_action: Implement one native DERP source-loading adapter covering URL admission, status/body handling and selected JSON/YAML receiver semantics.

findings.title: OIDC issuer configuration uses different URL grammar
findings.impact: WHATWG parsing trims inputs including leading control/space that Go URL parsing rejects during configuration, changing failure phase or optional-provider fallback.
findings.next_action: Add strict native validation/projection at the production configuration boundary; preserve generic embedding behavior and public signatures.

findings.title: Native HTTP response-header profile is still Hyper default
findings.impact: Native ACME clients retain H1 100-header and 417792-byte buffer limits and H2 16-KiB header-list limits versus Go default 10-MiB response-header budget. H1 obsolete folded-header acceptance also differs.
findings.next_action: Configure one native H1/H2 response-header/parser profile with the pinned budget/grammar; keep ordinary Hyper defaults unchanged.

findings.title: Implicit H1 body drop publishes retirement late
findings.impact: Incoming drops its channel before its consumer guard publishes Early. A concurrent driver can perform a small opportunistic drain before seeing retirement; the separate driver verdict still blocks reuse.
findings.next_action: Publish the selected early-drop verdict before channel destruction using a coherent private ownership change; retain explicit Close and pool acknowledgement.

findings.title: Closed H1 EOF can wait for an unnecessary write deadline
findings.impact: go_finish_eof can enter flush/50-ms writer wait for a connection already known nonreusable/closed. Go alive=false short-circuits wroteRequest and acknowledges read-loop exit.
findings.next_action: Decide nonreuse before writer waiting and preserve the bounded wait only for eligible reuse.

findings.title: Native startup/request/ACME diagnostic events remain different
findings.impact: Missing selected startup version/minimum-version fields, insecure remote-gRPC warning, per-request events and per-attempt ACME failure/status/body events. The three TLS scheme warnings already have implementations and are excluded.
findings.next_action: Implement a single native event/logging contract, preserving provider response bodies and sensitive-data handling, then compare output once after implementation batches.

assurance.title: Real-client PR/push filters omit seven vendored HTTP/TLS packages
assurance.detail: Only vendor/sqlx-core and vendor/sqlx-postgres are included. A change confined to h2, Hyper, Hyper-util, HyperRustls, Rustls, aws-lc-rs or instant-acme can skip the path-filtered real-client workflow; scheduled/manual execution remains configured.
assurance.next_action: Cover every production vendor patch in the workflow trigger/enforcement metadata in one CI change.

assurance.title: Historical paired reports do not establish the frozen source state
assurance.detail: Inspected reports contain Go version/case results but no source-tree/dirty-diff or binary fingerprint sufficient to bind current WIP and all local vendor patches. The old passing reports are useful historical evidence, not qualification of this freeze.
assurance.next_action: Have the final qualification run record source, vendor, binary, toolchain, platform, feature and backend fingerprints with paired results.

scope_decisions.title: OIDC/Noise resource-policy differences
scope_decisions.detail: OIDC discovery/UserInfo/JWKS have a 1-MiB cap; callbacks have a 128-permit limit; provider calls use 30-second deadlines; crypto workers are bounded. Noise also imposes a full-body deadline. These are deliberate bounds, not proof of Go-equivalent acceptance/timing. OAuth token response prefix limiting is separately Go-shaped. Resolve/document the compatibility policy instead of silently removing hardening.

scope_decisions.title: DERP IDs exceed current public u16 representation
scope_decisions.detail: SourceDerpMap and public DERP projection cannot represent IDs such as 70000 that the selected Go int representation can hold. Requires an additive native wide-ID design under the public-field compatibility constraint.

scope_decisions.title: Raw byte/path/error representation
scope_decisions.detail: Non-UTF-8 secret paths/content/environment and lower URI/DNS/TLS/OS error identities remain different or unqualified. Separate reachable native input support from generic custom driver/error surfaces.

scope_decisions.title: Cross-runtime default HTTP pool sharing
scope_decisions.detail: Native ACME accounts share within a production runtime; this does not provide Go process-wide DefaultTransport ownership across multiple Rust runtimes. Normal single-runtime serve and arbitrary embedding should have separate acceptance statements.

scope_decisions.title: Go runtime observability is substituted, not implemented
scope_decisions.detail: The /debug/pprof profile/trace handlers return Rust informational text, and symbol returns num_symbols:0. They are not a Go pprof CPU/heap/trace implementation. Choose useful tooling-compatible Rust profiling or explicitly exclude these runtime-specific endpoints from exact replacement claims.

scope_decisions.title: Generic Postgres driver corners are not all Headscale requirements
scope_decisions.detail: Custom codecs/explicit prepare/execute_many, missing FunctionCallResponse/CopyBoth variants, arbitrary ReadyForQuery statuses and invalid-byte metadata differ or remain unqualified. Concrete example: Rust rejects unknown transaction status while selected pgproto3 stores its byte. No normal Headscale SQL producing these backend messages was established. Cancellation/async cleanup differs at driver level; upstream ordinary DB mutations do not thread request contexts, and Rust durable mutations are shielded, so production reachability must be shown before treating every driver difference as a release blocker.
scope_decisions.evidence: vendor/sqlx-postgres/src/message/ready_for_query.rs:27; message/mod.rs:96; connection/mod.rs:192; headscale-db/src/lib.rs:572; selected pgproto3/ready_for_query.go:17; hscontrol/db/db.go:1185

security.title: Optional admin JSON mutation routes accept cookie sessions without CSRF validation
security.detail: guard_api accepts an authenticated session; JSON mutation handlers such as api_machines_expire do not call check_csrf, and read_json does not enforce JSON Content-Type. HTML forms do have CSRF checks. SameSite=Lax limits cross-site requests, but does not replace a same-site/untrusted-sibling origin check. This is a conditional exposure to investigate/repair when admin::router is mounted, not a demonstrated native serve authorization bypass.
security.reachability: Native serve production_extra_routes mounts the upstream grpc_gateway router, not this optional GUI router (headscale-cli/src/server.rs:2019).
security.next_action: Require an explicit anti-CSRF/origin/content-type contract for session-authenticated extension mutations, preserving bearer-only upstream gateway behavior.

security.title: Local vendor/crypto maintenance and current advisory status are unqualified
security.detail: Nine locally patched packages are selected by root Cargo.toml. Original pins/licenses/provenance are retained, but upstream security fixes will need deliberate comparison against local changes. CI config contains advisory/license/source jobs and a lockfile-only RUSTSEC-2023-0071 exception; those files are not evidence of a current clean graph or a security audit. Custom native TLS/JSON/PEM/bcrypt/HTTP/SQL adapters need focused review and final feature/backend validation.
security.reachability: Production native server, ACME, OIDC and database paths; optional extensions separately.
security.next_action: Perform the fresh dependency/advisory and vendor-delta security qualification in the final authorized validation phase. No new dependency versions or advisory claims in this audit.

qualification.requirement: Current workspace, admin/full, wire-only, H1-only/H2-only native/default combinations and selected crypto/backend profiles; sibling Octra wire-only integration remains a distinct boundary.
Refresh paired policy/ACL/SSH fixtures and stock-client registration, lifecycle, routes, DNS, map-stream omission/churn and revocation behavior on the final source state.

SQLite and Postgres fresh/imported v0.28/v0.29 historical shapes, Rust-to-Go and Go-to-Rust reopen, keys/users/routes/sessions, mutation/restart, sequence/NULL/timestamp state, interrupted migration, failed/ambiguous commit/rollback and sidecar/backup recovery.

Final exact CLI/error/startup output, configured gRPC/Unix/TLS/ACME/provider/DNS/DERP listener topology, HTTP framing/body/header/cancellation and shutdown cases; existing source adapters are not runtime proof.
Current active dependency/advisory/license graph, default isolation, vendor patches and crypto boundary, package contents, CA behavior, both container recipes and operator-facing exposure.

One final paired qualification packet bound to exact source/vendor/binary/toolchain/feature/platform/backend fingerprints; preserve failed cases and unknowns. Do not infer completion from scenario counts.

completion: Incomplete. No acceptance gate is closed by this audit. Finding count is an audit inventory, not an exact patch count or proof no further defect exists.

implementation_progress.method: Initial grouped source work used source/hash/direct rustfmt only. After user authorization, Cargo update/fetch resolved compatible dependency upgrades and vendor rebases. No tests/builds/lints/validators/probes/fixture capture/advisory qualification.

source_residuals.F07: Linux/Android and nix-supported BSD/Apple have event wakeups/rewatch plus content recovery. Windows/Solaris/illumos/AIX and other unsupported event targets retain polling; exact coalescing/backoff/resource/timing behavior remains unqualified.
source_residuals.F12: Finite YAML typed diagnostic aggregation/continuation and later-fatal precedence are now source implemented alongside canonical representation and JSON/encoding fixes. Remaining: granit versus Go scanner/parser syntax/property spans, mid-rune raw-byte previews and invalid binary strings normalized into Rust String, complex generic merge-key fatal formatting, other architecture casts, backend errors and nondeterministic text ordering. No runtime qualification.
source_residuals.F14: User authorized dependency upgrades. Local http1.5.0 with default-off coupled u32 index/hash capacity feature is selected through native SDK/root override; both container license copies are wired. Header/profile/resource behavior remains unbuilt and runtime-unqualified.
source_residuals.F17: Merged main-listener gateway/challenge/control plus inner Noise and raw/spawned Noise/DERP upgrade events, and parsed-URI/transport/status ACME observation are implemented. Body-poll counts differ from Go ResponseWriter.Write returned n; physical socket byte counters are not a substitute for that buffered application-write contract. Physical I/O/error/cancellation scheduling and raw-byte/error rendering remain narrower or unqualified.
